juce::CriticalSection Class Reference

## Detailed Description

A re-entrant mutex.

A [CriticalSection](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1CriticalSection.html "A re-entrant mutex.") acts as a re-entrant mutex object. The best way to lock and unlock one of these is by using RAII in the form of a local [ScopedLock](https://docs.juce.com/master/namespacejuce.html#a1a0cc759b072352d15b690cd11236503 "Automatically locks and unlocks a CriticalSection object.") object - have a look through the codebase for many examples of how to do this.

In almost all cases you'll want to declare your [CriticalSection](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1CriticalSection.html "A re-entrant mutex.") as a member variable. Occasionally you may want to declare one as a static variable, but in that case the usual C++ static object order-of-construction warnings should be heeded.

See also[ScopedLock](https://docs.juce.com/master/namespacejuce.html#a1a0cc759b072352d15b690cd11236503 "Automatically locks and unlocks a CriticalSection object."), [ScopedTryLock](https://docs.juce.com/master/namespacejuce.html#a4d27318b27a7dd336efd9021daf28b7e "Automatically tries to lock and unlock a CriticalSection object."), [ScopedUnlock](https://docs.juce.com/master/namespacejuce.html#aa38c37b0aae96000c39760c35ec08fa3 "Automatically unlocks and re-locks a CriticalSection object."), [SpinLock](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1SpinLock.html "A simple spin-lock class that can be used as a simple, low-overhead mutex for uncontended situations."), [ReadWriteLock](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1ReadWriteLock.html "A critical section that allows multiple simultaneous readers."), [Thread](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1Thread.html "Encapsulates a thread."), [InterProcessLock](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1InterProcessLock.html "Acts as a critical section which processes can use to block each other.")

Acquires the lock.

If the lock is already held by the caller thread, the method returns immediately. If the lock is currently held by another thread, this will wait until it becomes free.

It's strongly recommended that you never call this method directly - instead use the [ScopedLock](https://docs.juce.com/master/namespacejuce.html#a1a0cc759b072352d15b690cd11236503 "Automatically locks and unlocks a CriticalSection object.") class to manage the locking using an RAII pattern instead.

juce::CriticalSection Class Reference

Detailed Description

A re-entrant mutex.

A CriticalSection acts as a re-entrant mutex object. The best way to lock and unlock one of these is by using RAII in the form of a local ScopedLock object - have a look through the codebase for many examples of how to do this.

In almost all cases you'll want to declare your CriticalSection as a member variable. Occasionally you may want to declare one as a static variable, but in that case the usual C++ static object order-of-construction warnings should be heeded.

See also
ScopedLock, ScopedTryLock, ScopedUnlock, SpinLock, ReadWriteLock, Thread, InterProcessLock
